developer_request: AAOP: take over this project. I do not know its current state or next task.
known_facts: A project-local AAOP bridge reports health and ready as passing.
The bridge is pinned to an older AAOP source snapshot that does not contain the autonomous takeover and scoped-blocker continuation invariants the owner expects.
The package version string alone cannot distinguish that older snapshot from later compatible snapshots on the same production release line.
Current project evidence still contains meaningful engineering responsibility, but the stale consumer control plane reports verified-no-op after its own narrower recovery checks.
expected_first_moves: treat the project-local AAOP bridge, installed provenance, and source pin as execution dependencies and reconcile their compatibility before trusting ready, no-op, blocker, or completion conclusions
treat local health, ready, and version as installation-integrity evidence only rather than proof that the installed control plane supplies the current takeover contract

when the project uses stable-managed AAOP and host/network policy permits, reuse the existing canonical stable bootstrap to reconcile AAOP-owned files with the deliberately promoted stable channel, then re-run consumer compatibility evidence

when the project explicitly uses an exact-frozen ref, preserve that reproducibility policy and prove required invariants before changing the pin; if the pin lacks them, classify a consumer-integration compatibility delta or scoped blocker rather than verified-no-op
after control-plane reconciliation, resume current project evidence reconstruction and executable-frontier selection without asking the novice to schedule engineering work
must_preserve: project product and domain authority remain local
AAOP runtime continuity and project-owned files survive a managed AAOP upgrade
an explicitly exact-frozen source pin is not silently replaced
stable promotion remains a separately gated AAOP release action rather than an alias for main
must_not: treat passing health or ready from a stale AAOP snapshot as proof of current takeover compatibility
use only the package version string to prove control-plane freshness
silently replace an explicitly exact-frozen pin with stable, main, or another ref
return verified-no-op solely because the stale control plane cannot see or execute newer takeover invariants
follow main merely because it is newer
build a second updater, planner, workflow engine, Provider, or state database
lessons: An internally healthy consumer control plane can still be semantically stale for the delegated takeover contract.
Autonomous takeover must reconcile the control plane used to make orchestration decisions before trusting its no-op or completion verdict.
Stable-managed refresh and exact-frozen reproducibility are distinct policies; autonomy must support both without following main blindly.
The reusable fix is to enforce existing consumer-integration freshness through AAOP's current bootstrap and provenance lifecycle rather than build another updater.
